introduction: An elliptical metal pavilion was developed as a freestanding entrance feature for a high-end retail setting. Rolled upper ring beams, straight steel ties and slim paired posts establish the shape, while the curved fascia cladding and base pieces follow the oval perimeter. The workshop photographs record the full-size pre-assembly and the fit of the post heads, curved fascia transitions and lower returns before site work.

sections.title: A freestanding oval entrance frame with curved perimeter trim
paragraphs: The assembly brings the rolled upper rings, steel ties, paired posts and curved lower plinth into one opening. The fascia sheets and infill follow the outer ring, while the paired posts leave the central entrance clear. The scope shown here is fabrication and full-scale workshop verification.

sections.title: Close the oval while keeping the opening and joints aligned
paragraphs: The upper and lower curves must resolve to the same post positions. That relationship is important at the head of the assembly, where ring segments, panel edges and straight ties converge.

points.title: Ring closure
points.text: The two curved bands have to meet at their split joints without interrupting the oval profile or shifting the fascia line.

points.title: Post-head interfaces
points.text: The post heads receive both the curved framing and the straight ties. A full-size fit lets the team inspect closely spaced connections together.

points.title: Finish and base continuity
points.text: At the top and bottom, the visible edge must follow the perimeter into the post trim while allowing the pieces to be assembled in sequence.

sections.title: Rolled ring segments, straight ties and curved bases
paragraphs: The underside views show the rolled rings in relation to the cross ties. At the post head, a boxed junction connects the straight and curved members within the same depth of framing.
The lower radius piece sits between post groups. Its photographed fit makes it possible to compare the lower line with the plan shape of the ring above.

sections.title: Assemble the complete ellipse at full height in the workshop
paragraphs: The pavilion stood at full height so the workshop team could see the curved fascia, post groups, diagonal ties and base segments as one assembly. Front and oblique views show the stepped layers of the fascia and how the vertical members relate to the base radius.
The underside views show the perimeter from inside the opening. This angle reveals changes of plane at the fascia and the way the upper bands meet the post heads.

gallery.caption: The oblique view shows the relationship between the oval fascia above and the curved base below.

gallery.caption: From inside the frame, the curved upper bands and vertical posts can be viewed together across the span.

gallery.alt: Oblique underside view of an assembled pavilion ring and steel ties
gallery.caption: Looking upward from one side makes the junction of the two ring bands and diagonal ties visible.

sections.title: Follow the fascia return and its connections into the posts
paragraphs: Close workshop views show the angled fascia return and the transition from outer trim to curved infill at the post head. An underside view shows where the inner band and steel tie approach the same node.
At floor level, the curved plinth ends against a post group. This junction shows how the exposed trim returns into the foot of the upright during fit-up.

gallery.caption: The lower return shows how the curved base terminates against the post group while the frame is still in the workshop.

gallery.caption: The close-up records the angled meeting line at the fascia return and the post head.

gallery.caption: The junction shows the transition between the finished outer trim, curved infill panel and inner framing.

gallery.alt: Underside view of the ring joint and paired upright ends
gallery.caption: From below, the boxed connection makes the alignment between the two ring edges and upright ends visible.

sections.title: Specify the oval, its supports and the assembly route
paragraphs: An elliptical layout benefits from a coordinated plan, elevation and node sections so the visible joints can be reviewed against the hidden supports.

points.title: Setting-out drawings
points.text: Provide CAD or PDF plans with the oval axes, post positions and opening dimensions. Add head-node and base sections with available anchoring points.

points.title: Finish sample and joint intent
points.text: Sequence the visible split joints and set their look in the fascia sample. Confirm which junctions require access and which should read as a continuous line.

points.title: Transport and venue access
points.text: Check delivery routes, door openings, headroom and limits on temporary supports before agreeing how to divide the ring and lower plinth for handling.

conclusion: A full-size workshop assembly lets a curved retail entrance be reviewed from the overall oval down to each post head and fascia joint. The same approach applies to custom portals where a thin curved enclosure has to meet a controlled opening. Send a CAD or PDF plan and sections with the finish and access requirements to scope a representative trial.
